api/api/GameFramework.Config.Enums.Confi.summary: Enum ConfigFlags Behavioral flags that control how configuration variables are handled Can be combined using bitwise OR to give variables multiple behaviors Usage Examples: Flags.Save: Variable persists between sessions Flags.Save | Flags.ServerInfo: Variable persists AND is sent to clients Flags.Cheat: Variable can only be modified when cheats are enabled Namespace: GameFramework.Config.Enums Assembly: .dll Syntax [Flags] public enum ConfigFlags Fields Name Description Cheat Variable is considered a cheat and can only be modified when cheats are enabled Used for debug variables, god mode, infinite resources, etc. Provides protection against accidental or unauthorized modifications ClientInfo Variable is sent from client to server when connecting or when value changes Used for client preferences that server needs to know: preferred name, color, etc. Allows server to customize experience based on client preferences None Default behavior - temporary variable, not saved or replicated Save Variable should be saved to configuration file and loaded on startup Used for user preferences, graphics settings, key bindings, etc. Triggers file I/O operations when modified ServerInfo Variable is sent from server to clients when they connect or when value changes Used for server settings that affect gameplay: time limits, player counts, etc. Ensures all clients have consistent server configuration User Variable was created dynamically by user (not predefined in code) Used for custom variables created through console or scripting May have different validation or cleanup behavior

api/api/GameFramework.Core.DiContainer.h.summary: Class DiContainer Enhanced dependency injection container with automatic constructor injection support. Supports singleton registration, factory registration, type bindings, and automatic dependency resolution. Inheritance object DiContainer Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Namespace: GameFramework.Core Assembly: .dll Syntax public class DiContainer Remarks This DI container provides three main registration patterns: Singleton: One instance created and reused for all requests Transient: New instance created for each request Factory: Custom factory function called for each request The container automatically resolves constructor dependencies using reflection, selecting the constructor with the most parameters and recursively resolving all dependencies. Circular dependency detection prevents infinite resolution loops. Design Benefits: Clean separation of concerns, automatic dependency resolution, easy testing, loose coupling Trade-offs: Runtime dependency resolution, potential circular dependencies, reflection overhead Examples // Register services container.RegisterSingleton<ILogger, ConsoleLogger>(); container.RegisterTransient<IRepository, DatabaseRepository>(); container.RegisterFactory<IConnection>(() => new SqlConnection(connectionString)); // Resolve services (automatic constructor injection) var service = container.Resolve<IMyService>(); Properties Instance Gets the singleton instance of the DI container. Declaration public void RegisterFactory<T>(Func<T> factory) where T : class Parameters Type Name Description Func<T> factory The factory function that creates instances of T. Type Parameters Name Description T The service type to register. Remarks Use factory registration when you need custom creation logic, configuration, or when each request should receive a fresh instance with specific setup. The factory function is called every time the service is resolved. Examples container.RegisterFactory<IDatabase>(() => new SqlDatabase(GetConnectionString())); container.RegisterFactory<IHttpClient>(() => new HttpClient { Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30) }); Exceptions Type Condition ArgumentNullException Thrown when factory is null. RegisterSingleton<T>() Registers a singleton for a concrete type (no interface mapping). Examples var logger = new FileLogger("/logs/app.log"); container.RegisterSingleton<ILogger>(logger); Exceptions Type Condition ArgumentNullException Thrown when instance is null. RegisterSingleton<TInterface, TImplementation>() Registers a singleton mapping from interface to implementation type. The instance will be created on first request using constructor injection. Declaration public void RegisterSingleton<TInterface, TImplementation>() where TImplementation : class, TInterface Type Parameters Name Description TInterface The service interface type. TImplementation The concrete implementation type. Remarks The implementation instance is created lazily on first request and then cached for all subsequent requests. Constructor dependencies are automatically resolved. Examples container.RegisterSingleton<IUserService, DatabaseUserService>(); // First call creates instance, subsequent calls return cached instance var service1 = container.Resolve<IUserService>(); var service2 = container.Resolve<IUserService>(); // Same instance as service1 RegisterTransient<TInterface, TImplementation>() Registers a transient type binding where a new instance is created for each request. api/api/GameFramework.Core.GameContext.h.summary: Class GameContext Centralized context object that provides access to all core game services through dependency injection. This class serves as a service aggregator that collects all essential game systems into a single, easily injectable dependency for game states and other complex systems. Inheritance object GameContext Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Namespace: GameFramework.Core Assembly: .dll Syntax public class GameContext Remarks The GameContext follows the Context Object pattern, providing a clean way to pass multiple related services to classes that need access to various game systems. Rather than injecting each service individually, classes can inject the GameContext and access all services through it.
